title: Rapid identification of bacterial viability, culturable and non-culturable stages by using flow cytometry
protocol: Stain bacterial samples according to the protocol referred to in Step 3 of ‘Preparation of probed samples’.
Apply 2.5 ml of each membrane permeable probe (SYTO 9, SYTO 13, SYTO 17, and SYTO 40) at received concentrations to the diluted pure cultures separately.
Analyze samples stained with SYTO 9, SYTO 13, SYTO 17, and SYTO 40 by FCM.

Assess FCM parameters including degree of staining, good emission signals, low false signals (from debris), and optimum number of events of cells displayed in FCM histograms to determine optimal probes for each strain.
Compare the effectiveness of PI, SYTOX Blue, and 7-AAD to confirm that PI is the best choice for detecting dead cells (those with damaged membranes).
Plate an aliquot of cells in late log phase after exposure to membrane impermeable probes on standard nutrient agar.
Plate an aliquot of unexposed cells in late log phase on standard nutrient agar.
Assess the optimal incubation time of PI, SYTOX Blue, and 7-AAD using an epifluorescence microscope.
Run liquid counting beads with bacterial cells.
Compare the number of events detected by FCM.
Determine optimal voltage settings of the PMT for emission spectra.
Separate bead region from cell region in side-scatter vs. respective emission spectra.
Verify bead concentration provided by manufacturer.
Cells at concentrations greater than ~10^4/ml cause high abort rates in FCM.
Concentrations less than ~10^4/ml result in interference with sheath fluid electronic signal.
Avoid false-positive signals during staining.
Vortex pure culture samples for 2 minutes.
Dilute pure culture samples with appropriate broth to obtain a cell number close to ~10^4/ml.
Pass 10 to 15 ml of diluted stained cells through a sterilized 0.20 μm pore-size and 25-mm-diameter hydrophilic membrane.
Observe captured cells on the membrane under an epifluorescence microscope.
Run a specific amount of liquid counting beads in appropriate broth dilution media and purified NP water separately to identify noise effect from debris in growth media.
Vortex samples of pure cultures of different cells for 2 min.
Dilute samples of pure cultures with appropriate broth to obtain a cell number close to 10^4/ml.
Observe cells under the epifluorescence microscope to ensure that clumping has not occurred.
Plate 50 µl in triplicate of serial dilutions on respective agar.
Incubate plates at 37 °C for 20 h.
Add 2.5 µl of each fluorescent probe (SYTO 9, SYTO 13, SYTO 17, and SYTO 40) separately to 1 ml of diluted individual samples.
Vortex samples for 30 sec.
Incubate samples in the dark for 60 min.
Prepare the probes immediately after thawing and avoid light exposure during thawing.
Complete area scaling and quality control adjustments prior to running samples.
Quality control of the FCM must be done using CST beads before starting the FCM measurement.
Set voltage settings, threshold parameters, and flow rates according to Table S1 for each probe/cell combination.
Use fluorescence for thresholding.
Vary FSC and SSC parameters to set populations inside the histogram.
Optimize settings when different cells and probes are analyzed.
Save each setting and operating conditions for specific cells and probes.
Transfer a known volume of stained cells into a sterilized tube.
Add the appropriate amount of liquid counting beads to the sample.
Vortex the sample for 10 seconds.
Inject the sample into the FCM without changing settings and operating conditions as indicated in Table S1.
Analyze the number of events/sec in the acquired data set.
If fewer than 500 events/sec, add 25 μl of beads.
If more than 1000 events/sec, add 50 μl of beads.
Dilute stained cells 1 to 2-fold with appropriate broth if necessary.
Gate cells in forward scatter vs. side scatter plots.
Create a one-dimensional histogram gate for cells stained with a specific probe.
Create another one-dimensional histogram gate for the liquid counting bead region.
Display the gates in histograms to separate cell and bead regions.
Record the same number of total events for all conditions, typically 5000 events per case and run.
Calculate the number of cells per unit volume using the formula provided.
Acquire data from three or four independent experiments for each condition.
Use the same accurate pipette filler for adding probes and beads into the diluted cultures throughout the same experiment.
Count total cells (live and dead) using SYTO probes.
Enumerate dead cells using PI.
Calculate live cells by subtracting the number of PI-stained cells from that of SYTO-stained cells.
Estimate nonculturable cell numbers by subtracting the number of plate count (culturable) cells from that of live cells.
Dilute previously grown cultures in LB or King’s broth to a final concentration of 10^4 cell/ml.
Transfer 1-ml of these diluted cells into separate 2-ml sterilized culturing tubes.
Place the tubes containing the cells in a 72°C heat block with nanopure water.
Prepare multiple tubes for each diluted cell and for each heating condition.
Submerge tubes in hot water for 5 min.
Submerge tubes in hot water for 10 min.
Submerge tubes in hot water for 15 min.
Bring cells to room temperature (in 5 to 6 min).
Transfer two culture tubes of each treatment of each heat-exposed cells to an incubated shaker for 6 h.
Add 2.5 µl of propidium iodide (PI) at received concentration to 1-ml of heat exposed cells.
Incubate the cells in the dark for 60 min.
Inject the sample into the FCM.
Follow the same protocols for FCM analysis methods as used in the section entitled Flow cytometric analysis of SYTO probed samples.
Create two one-dimensional gates in the cell and bead regions in the respective histograms for each cell (either control or heat inactivated for different periods).
Calculate the number of cells in each heat inactivation condition using equation 1.
Prior to cell sorting, follow the initialization procedures as discussed in the section entitled Equipment Setup.
Sort the minor populations separately from the main population if they are represented in the shoulders of histograms.
Optimize voltage setups and threshold values for stained cells in the histograms.
Create two one-dimensional gates for the stained cells in the shouldering of the histograms and also for the major population in the symmetrical or asymmetrical distribution of histograms.
Stain 8 ml of diluted pure culture cells (~10^4 cell/ml) with respective SYTO probes.
Inject samples into FCM and sort.
Vortex material in 5-ml sterilized culture tubes and filter through two sterilized 0.20 μm pore size GE Osmonics, PCTE 25 mm diameter hydrophilic membranes.
Rinse the tubes with filtered fluorescence-activated cell sorter (FACS) flow sheath fluid several times to recover remaining cells from the tubes.
Filter rinsed material through respective membrane.
Collect populations from two one-dimensional gates in sorting chamber.
Place membranes under the calibrated epifluorescence microscope and observe to determine the accuracy of sorting.
Perform microscopic observation of cells on membrane surfaces as soon as possible before fluorescent intensities fade.
Place resulting membranes in PowerBead Tubes from the PowerSoil TM DNA isolation kit.
Extract DNA according to the manufacturer’s protocols within 30 min after sorting.
Warm the agarose gel solution with ethidium bromide for 2-4 minutes to liquify it.
Pour the liquified gel into the gel box using a laboratory grade mask.
Run samples on an agarose gel for 30 minutes at 94 volts.
Wash the gel with 1x TBE buffer for 2-5 minutes prior to imaging.
Take images using a FluroChem TM IS-8800 to estimate cell density in each sorted tube.
